bug_semantics: @cleverbrush/deep deepExtend recursively copies every enumerable source key into a fresh ordinary object without rejecting __proto__. From ece027428a9a5755916f159a5760665be9cc89a6 onward, the merge loop uses Reflect.has(o1, key). For attacker-controlled JSON containing an own __proto__ object, Reflect.has sees the inherited __proto__ accessor on an ordinary target; o1[key] resolves to Object.prototype, both sides satisfy the object checks, and extendObject recurses into Object.prototype. Attacker-chosen inner properties are then assigned as own properties of Object.prototype and become inherited by every ordinary object in the realm. An application reaches the sink by passing parsed request/config/query data to deepExtend; the resulting realm-wide inherited values can corrupt authorization or configuration logic, cause denial of service, or feed a secondary gadget. The disclosed working route is __proto__; constructor is a function on the ordinary receiver and therefore does not take this recursion branch, although the closing defense rejects __proto__, constructor, and prototype.
flaw_origin: The smallest true BIC is ece027428a9a5755916f159a5760665be9cc89a6, a normal one-parent source commit. In libs/deep/src/deepExtend.ts it replaced the parent's own-property decision !o1.hasOwnProperty(keys[i]) with the prototype-chain-aware !Reflect.has(o1, keys[i]) while retaining recursive descent and unfiltered property names. That semantic change made inherited __proto__ appear to be an existing object and redirected recursion into Object.prototype. The absence of an unsafe-key denylist was older, but the immediate parent assigned __proto__ on the local merge receiver instead of recursively writing attacker properties into Object.prototype, so the realm-wide primitive reported in issue #213 begins at this commit. Later commits only reformatted, typed, or documented the same vulnerable loop until the fix.
ai_marker: none: the raw BIC commit object has human author and committer Andrew Zolotukhin <andrewzolotukhin@gmail.com>, message 'feat(deep): improved deep library tests', and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer
evidence: First-party report https://github.com/cleverbrush/framework/issues/213 gives the 4.4.0 PoC deepExtend({ a: {} }, JSON.parse('{"a":{"__proto__":{"polluted":"pp"}}}')) and explains that Reflect.has follows the inherited __proto__ accessor, recursion receives Object.prototype, and a fresh object subsequently inherits polluted='pp'. The report identifies @cleverbrush/deep <=4.4.0 and the application-level sink condition of attacker-influenced input.

Run git show --no-ext-diff ece027428a9a5755916f159a5760665be9cc89a6 -- libs/deep/src/deepExtend.ts. The diff changes the parent loop from !o1.hasOwnProperty(keys[i]) to !Reflect.has(o1, keys[i]), preserves o1[keys[i]] object inspection and recursive extendObject(o1[keys[i]], o2[keys[i]]), and does not add an unsafe-key filter. This is the causal source edit, not a move, release commit, revert, merge, or squash aggregate.

Run git show b5315a6c04f5db1688ff14eb0f7c24da636a77d8:libs/deep/src/deepExtend.ts and compare it directly with the BIC. The parent tests !o1.hasOwnProperty('__proto__'); that is false for an ordinary receiver, so its assignment branch writes through the receiver's __proto__ setter and does not call extendObject with Object.prototype. The BIC's Reflect.has('__proto__') is true and therefore takes the recursive branch. This directly verifies absence of the disclosed realm-wide Object.prototype write in the immediate parent.

Run git log ece027428a9a5755916f159a5760665be9cc89a6 -L 35,63:libs/deep/src/deepExtend.ts and git log --all --reverse -S'Reflect.has(o1, keys[i])' -- libs/deep/src/deepExtend.ts. The line trace shows the earlier hasOwnProperty implementation and the BIC replacement; the pickaxe search returns only ece027428a9a5755916f159a5760665be9cc89a6 as addition and ef39f7651979dcccca05112e1247c002d61595d2 as removal. git blame -L 55,82 c047cae3311c2113221b63d07f1f5f452d795017 attributes the pre-fix Reflect.has branch and recursive call to ece027428a9a5755916f159a5760665be9cc89a6.

Run git cat-file -p ece027428a9a5755916f159a5760665be9cc89a6. It records exactly one parent, b5315a6c04f5db1688ff14eb0f7c24da636a77d8, human author and committer Andrew Zolotukhin <andrewzolotukhin@gmail.com>, and only the subject 'feat(deep): improved deep library tests'; there are no trailers or bot/AI markers. AI judgment is based only on this BIC commit object.

Run git for-each-ref --contains ece027428a9a5755916f159a5760665be9cc89a6 --sort=creatordate refs/tags and git show v1.1.1:libs/deep/package.json. The first containing release tag is v1.1.1 (2023-04-28), whose package manifest identifies @cleverbrush/deep version 1.1.1. The vulnerable BIC remains in every later deep release through @cleverbrush/deep@4.4.0; issue #213 independently confirms the published 4.4.0 artifact.

Run git show --no-ext-diff ef39f7651979dcccca05112e1247c002d61595d2 -- libs/deep/src/deepExtend.ts libs/deep/src/deepExtend.test.ts .changeset/fix-deep-extend-prototype-pollution.md. The direct fix skips __proto__, constructor, and prototype before lookup or assignment, changes Reflect.has to Object.hasOwn, removes the unsafe single-source return, adds top-level/nested pollution regression cases, and declares a patch release for @cleverbrush/deep.

Run git show -s --format='%H %P %s' ef39f7651979dcccca05112e1247c002d61595d2 c1412e490403fc60c236db29da6568b77c15a400 810398c1308c500c3b8b6af380b5a89371389327 fff3c9563f281614adb9020bfed87954194133a7. It reproduces the landing chain direct fix ef39f765 -> PR #214 merge c1412e4 -> advisory-cited master merge 810398c -> version-release merge fff3c956. git cat-file -p '@cleverbrush/deep@4.4.0' targets bca74e18b038a9a36e1aa6d2cf992a49bee775da, the first parent of 810398c and therefore still vulnerable; git cat-file -p '@cleverbrush/deep@4.4.1' targets fff3c9563f281614adb9020bfed87954194133a7. git tag --contains ef39f7651979dcccca05112e1247c002d61595d2 '@cleverbrush/deep@*' returns only 4.4.1 and 4.4.2, proving the fixed release boundary.

The bundle advisory names 810398c1308c500c3b8b6af380b5a89371389327 as the patch and directs users to upgrade from affected <=4.4.0 to 4.4.1. First-party PR #214 says it fixes issue #213, and PR #215 is the v4.4.1 bug-fix landing PR.
reasoning: The report's vulnerability is specifically a realm-wide Object.prototype pollution primitive, not merely the older behavior of changing the returned receiver's prototype. History establishes that ece027428a9a5755916f159a5760665be9cc89a6 first made the critical inherited-property lookup: Reflect.has finds __proto__, the inherited accessor produces Object.prototype, and recursive merge writes attacker keys there. Its direct parent uses hasOwnProperty and cannot enter that recursion for __proto__, so parent absence is proven. Line history and pickaxe converge on the same ordinary source commit; no decomposition is needed. The direct security change is ef39f7651979dcccca05112e1247c002d61595d2, while the advisory-cited closing master merge is 810398c1308c500c3b8b6af380b5a89371389327 and the fixed package begins at 4.4.1. Finally, the BIC commit object contains only a human identity and plain subject with no AI attribution or bot signal. Under the protocol, later activity and the fix are irrelevant to AI attribution, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
